literal: The great ocean of birth they will swim, they will not swim, the Lord's feet those who do not reach.
translation: Those who reach the feet of the Lord will swim across the great ocean of births; those who do not reach His feet will not.
modern: இறைவனுடைய திருவடிகளைப் பொருந்தி வணங்குபவர்கள் பிறவியாகிய பெரிய கடலைக் கடப்பார்கள்; அவனுடைய திருவடிகளைப் பொருந்தாதவர்கள் அந்தக் கடலைக் கடக்க மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares the cycle of continuous births and deaths to a vast, formidable ocean (peruṅkaṭal). The poet asserts that the only way to successfully swim across (nīntuvar) this ocean of existence is by seeking refuge at the feet of the Lord (iṟaivan aṭi). Those who fail to reach or surrender to those divine feet (cērātār) will remain trapped, unable to cross (nīntār) the sea of worldly existence. The metaphor of the ocean highlights the difficulty of escaping worldly suffering without spiritual guidance.
